plainLanguage: Garland still builds homes under the older 2015 International Residential Code, 2015 energy code and 2014 electrical code, not the 2021 editions most neighbors use. Most new homes are in the SF-7 district (7,000 sq ft lots); corner lots need 15 ft on the street side. Exact front, side and rear setbacks still need to be read from the city's table, so enter them from your plat. Garland requires one full bathroom and 120 sq ft of living area for every two bedrooms. The permit is $0.52 per sq ft of living area plus a 25% processing fee - about $1,560 for a 2,400 sq ft home. Add a water impact fee (about $593) and, in newer subdivisions, a $3,034 roadway impact fee. In a floodplain, the floor must be 2 ft above flood level. The city cannot require brick or stone, but your HOA might.
